answer_1.quote: text revision encompasses various subtasks (e.g., paraphrasing, summarization, text simplification, style transfer, grammar error correction (GEC))

answer_2.quote: text revision is assessed using well-established metrics such as ROUGE or BERTScore

answer_3.quote: We explore LLM-as-a-Judge approaches to evaluate both these aspects.

answer_4.quote: we designed an annotation task where human annotators compared pairs of revision candidates and selected their preferred version.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators answered a series of questions: • Q1A and Q1B Relatedness x2: Did model A/B address the instruction? {Yes strictly, Yes with additional modifications, No} • If it was your article and your instruction: -Q2 Correctness: Which revisions would you consider acceptable? {Both, A only, B only, None} -Q3 Preference: Which revision would you prefer to include in your paper? {Both, A, B, None} • Category-Specific Evaluation: -Rewriting light: Which model improves the academic style and English the most? -Rewriting medium: Which model improves the readability and structure the most? -Rewriting heavy: Which model improves the readability and clarity the most? -Concision: Which model manages the most to give a shorter version while keeping all the important ideas?
